subject: Short burst relief & measurement proposal for hosted API p50/p95
messages:
From: Tom Greene <tom.greene@brightpeakhealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@brightpeakhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Short holiday-batch window — ask on p95 handling

Hi Lauren,

Quick note from our ops team — during our year-end claims ingest (Nov 24–27, local US regions) we expect short bursts where request latency spikes for a 20–30 minute window each day. Our contract references a p95 target of 220ms for Hosted API but the recent load tests suggest transient p95s will exceed that during those bursts.

Can Redwood propose a temporary handling approach? Specifically we are looking for:
- short-term measurement carveout (20–30 min daily) or an alternate measurement window for those days;
- evidence we won’t see long-term degradation if you relax p95 for those short windows;
- any operational mitigations (fallback model, regional routing) you can commit to.

If helpful we can share traces and a sample histogram — attaching a small CSV excerpt.

Thanks,
Tom
VP Ops, BrightPeak Health
Attachment: burst_evidence.csv (CSV, 12KB)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Tom Greene <tom.greene@brightpeakhealth.com>

Date: 2026-11-15T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Short holiday-batch window — ask on p95 handling

Tom — thanks for the heads up and for the CSV. We can absolutely work through a short-term plan. High level next steps:

1) Internal technical assessment (Ben + Karthik) to validate evidence and propose measurement approach.
2) Proposed SLO amendment (timeboxed carveout vs window-shift) and concrete mitigation commitments.
3) If accepted, we’ll publish an addendum and set up a short canary for Nov 21–23 to validate.

I’m looping Ben and Karthik to scope the evidence we need and the draft amendment. Can you confirm the exact local time window you expect (EST/PST)? Also, please share any traces you have (sample spans) — the CSV helped.

Next update by EOD Tuesday.

—Lauren

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Short holiday-batch window — ask on p95 handling

Lauren / Ben — internal notes and proposed technical approach after reviewing burst_evidence.csv: 

Summary of data: daily 18:10–18:35 PST spikes (pattern: many parallel long-context requests causing KV-cache churn); p50 remains ~40–60ms, p95 jumps to 420–680ms for the 20–30 minute window. Outside the window p95 is stable at ~180–210ms.

Proposal (two tracks):
A) Measurement carveout (preferred): define a timeboxed daily carveout for Nov 24–27, 18:00–18:40 PST, where these samples are excluded from contractual p95 calculations. We’d limit carveout to those days and include a mandatory evidence package post-window showing no downstream degradation.

B) Window-shift (fallback): keep contractual window but apply a rolling 1-hour measurement window that downweights 5-minute extremes via percentile bucketing (e.g., requiring p95 across 12 5-minute sub-buckets). This is more permanent and needs legal review.

Operational mitigations we can commit to during carveout:
- Canary traffic routing to alternative GPU pool for affected region (activation within 10 minutes).
- Autoscaling guard: raise burst headroom to +20% for the window.
- Temporary model fallback to a slightly smaller quantized variant for latency-sensitive calls (same correctness tests).

Required evidence from BrightPeak: request/trace samples for two days (we have one), and a histogram per-minute aggregate for the affected window. Once we have those we can prepare a 1–pager amendment (attached as measurement-plan.pdf draft) and a short runbook for activation.

I attached a draft measurement-plan.pdf and a proposed SLO amendment (slo-amendment-draft.docx). If you sign off internally we can convert to an addendum and route to legal.

—Karthik
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
Attachment: measurement-plan.pdf; slo-amendment-draft.docx
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Tom Greene <tom.greene@brightpeakhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Short holiday-batch window — ask on p95 handling (proposal)

Tom — thanks for the patience. Attached is a concise proposal based on our review. Key points: 

- Timeboxed carveout: Nov 24–27, 18:00–18:40 PST daily (20 minute core window + 10 minute guard). During these carveout windows samples will be excluded from the contractual p95 calculation for Hosted API for this account only.
- Operational commitments during carveout: activate regional canary (within 10 mins), enable +20% burst headroom autoscale, and automatic fallback to the quantized model if p95 exceeds 500ms for two consecutive 5-minute buckets.
- Evidence & audit: BrightPeak to provide per-minute histograms for each day; Redwood will deliver a post-run report within 48 hours showing per-bucket behavior and confirmation of mitigations applied.
- Duration & rollback: carveout applies only to Nov 24–27. If post-run report shows persistent degradation outside the window, the carveout will be rescinded and we’ll immediately open a remediation plan.

Attachments: measurement-plan.pdf, slo-amendment-draft.docx, burst_evidence.csv
HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

If this aligns, reply with approval and we’ll route the amendment to legal + send the technical runbook to your ops contact for test traffic on Nov 21–23.

Best,
Lauren
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: measurement-plan.pdf (PDF, 28KB); slo-amendment-draft.docx (DOCX, 14KB); burst_evidence.csv (CSV, 12KB)
